overlay.$description: Modal/dialog scrim. Deliberately derived via color-mix() at the semantic layer rather than adding an alpha primitive to Token Foundation — see Semantic Layer roadmap Chunk 01.

inverse.$description: Text on solid dark backgrounds, e.g. on a primary button.

danger.$description: Real WCAG contrast computed against surface.base, not assumed: 11.99:1 light / 10.16:1 dark (color.danger.9, the solid-background step, also passes at 6.45:1 light / 5.59:1 dark, but step 11 matches this family's own convention — text always uses 11/12, never 9 — and clears AAA (7:1) with real margin where step 9 barely would in dark mode. See decisions/decision-feedback-text-colors.md.

warning.$description: 13.65:1 light / 11.13:1 dark against surface.base. Same reasoning as text.danger.

success.$description: 11.25:1 light / 10.52:1 dark against surface.base. Same reasoning as text.danger.

primary-active.$description: Reuses hover's value — the primitive step convention has no dedicated pressed step (9-10 are solid bg default/hover, 11-12 are reserved for text). Pressed feedback comes from motion, not a third color. See Semantic Layer roadmap Chunk 02.

primary-disabled.$description: Flattened to neutral, not a dimmed brand color — a washed-out brand green still reads as "branded"; flat neutral reads unambiguously as "not interactive".

success.$description: Deliberately NOT {color.brand.9} — a dedicated hue (140°, higher chroma) so a success signal never blends into ordinary brand chrome. See Semantic Layer roadmap Chunk 03.

success-subtle.$description: Banner/toast backgrounds behind step-9 text or icons.

ring.$description: Reuses the brand color — unlike feedback colors, a focus ring's job never competes with "is this branded chrome," so there's no signal-collision risk here.
